answer: A sparrow carries only its own seed, so credit cannot be pooled across a flock. Each identity needs two holders outside its own dune to countersign its passage, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n separate witnesses instead of a single ring. Every voyage is priced by rank: the k-th passage an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still requiring unrelated guarantors. An audit re-walks a random dune each epoch, and an unconfirmed passage voids the whole route and forfeits its bonds.
